chunks: Saʿd narrated from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Aʿraj, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I trim my nails, my moustache, and shave my head; must I perform ghusl? He said: No, there is no ghusl upon you. I said: Then should I perform wudu (ablution)? He said: No, there is no wudu (ablution) upon you. I said: Then should I wipe water over my nails? He said: It is pure; there is no wiping required upon you.

key_terms.طَهُورٌ: pure and not requiring purification due to this act
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: ritual bath required for certain states
key_terms.مَسْحٌ: wiping, here meaning a purificatory wiping with water

ai.seo_question: Does trimming nails, cutting the moustache, or shaving the head require ghusl or wudu (ablution) in Shi'i fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that trimming the nails, taking from the moustache, and shaving the head do not make ghusl or wudu (ablution) obligatory. It also states that no special wiping of water over the nails is required, affirming the continuing taharah of the body after such acts.
